observation.visible_scene: A clear cylindrical glass stands on a white surface against a teal wall. Inside it are two stacked liquid layers: a clear layer filling the lower half and a yellow/olive layer occupying a band in the middle. A yellow straw rests inside, its lower tip fixed at the bottom center of the glass, with the upper part extending above the rim and out of the top of the frame. The straw's submerged portion appears laterally displaced and 'broken' at the air/oil and oil/water interfaces (refraction through the curved glass and the oil layer), so the air segment, the oil-band segment, and the water segment do not line up into a single straight line.
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the straw rotates about its fixed base: its top end drifts steadily from a near-vertical position (frame 1) to a pronounced leftward lean (frame 41), while the bottom tip stays at the same spot at the base of the glass.

As the straw tilts, the three refracted visual segments shift accordingly—the air segment moves left at the top, and the apparent kinks at the oil and water boundaries move with it—but the lower tip remains anchored.
The glass, the two liquid layers, the white surface line, and the teal background remain in fixed positions, indicating the camera is static and the only motion is the straw's rotation.
outside_clip_unknowns: No hand or other object is visible pushing or pulling the straw, so the cause and agent of the tilt are unseen.
The straw's full length above the rim is cropped out, so its true orientation and any motion above the frame edge are unknown.
What precedes the tilt (whether the straw was already being moved at the crop start) and what follows after the clip ends are not shown.
uncertain_details: The exact angle of the straw is hard to read because refraction makes the in-liquid segments appear offset from the real straight straw; the apparent 'breaks' are optical, not separate pieces.
Whether the base tip is truly motionless or merely appears so within frame precision is not fully verifiable, though it stays within the same small region throughout.
